341	\paragraph{(1) Depth signal persists at 7--8B scale.}
342	Both 7--8B models substantially exceed the 25\% chance baseline: Llama-3.1-8B achieves 70.2\% (95\% CI $[68.3, 72.4]$) and Qwen2.5-7B achieves 60.1\% ($[58.0, 62.1]$), confirming that recursive depth remains estimable from perplexity-based features even when the generator is 5--7$\times$ larger than the reference model.
343	Depth-0 separability is preserved in both models: d0v1 AUC is 0.949 (Llama-3.1) and 0.969 (Qwen2.5).
344	
345	\paragraph{(2) EDD at 7--8B scale.}
346	At threshold $T{=}0.70$, Qwen2.5-7B maintains all consecutive-pair AUCs above 0.70 through depth~5 (Table~\ref{tab:cross_scale_auc}), yielding $\mathrm{EDD}_{T{=}0.70} > 5$---exceeding the $\mathrm{EDD}{=}4$ observed at 1--1.5B.
347	Llama-3.1-8B matches the smaller models at $\mathrm{EDD}{=}4$: its monotonic decay causes d4v5 (0.618) to drop below $T$, despite stronger signal at shallower depths.
348	Both larger generators produce weaker per-step signal than the 1--1.5B models (mean consecutive AUC: 0.786 for Llama-3.1, 0.782 for Qwen2.5, vs.\ 0.852 at 1--1.5B).
349	
350	\begin{table}[h]
351	\centering
352	\small
353	\caption{Consecutive binary AUC for 7--8B models (nucleus $p{=}0.95$). Llama-3.1-8B exhibits monotonic decay (d4v5 drops below $T{=}0.70$); Qwen2.5-7B shows a non-monotonic (U-shaped) pattern with all pairs above $T$.}
354	\label{tab:cross_scale_auc}
355	\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccc@{}}
356	\toprule
357	Model & d0v1 & d1v2 & d2v3 & d3v4 & d4v5 \\
358	\midrule
359	Llama-3.1-8B & 0.949 & 0.877 & 0.771 & 0.716 & 0.618 \\
360	Qwen2.5-7B & 0.969 & 0.729 & 0.709 & 0.732 & 0.772 \\
361	\bottomrule
362	\end{tabular}
363	\end{table}
364	
365	\paragraph{(3) Divergent AUC trajectories and instruction-tuning effect.}
366	Among instruction-tuned models, Llama-3.1-8B exhibits monotonic AUC decay consistent with the 1--1.5B pattern, while Qwen2.5-7B shows a U-shaped recovery beyond d2v3 (Table~\ref{tab:cross_scale_auc}).
367	A base-model control (Llama-3.1-8B without instruction tuning) clarifies the causal direction: the base model achieves 59.9\% four-class accuracy (95\% CI [57.8, 62.15], $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}2$) with non-monotonic AUC decay (Table~\ref{tab:llama3_base_auc}), while the instruction-tuned variant reaches 70.2\% with strictly monotonic decay.
368	The base-model control experiment suggests instruction-tuning regularizes rather than confounds the depth signal.
369	
370	\begin{table}[h]
371	\centering
372	\small
373	\caption{Pairwise AUC: Llama-3.1-8B Base vs.\ Instruct.}
374	\label{tab:llama3_base_auc}
375	\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
376	\toprule
377	Variant & $d_{0\text{v}1}$ & $d_{1\text{v}2}$ & $d_{2\text{v}3}$ & $d_{3\text{v}4}$ & $d_{4\text{v}5}$ \\
378	\midrule
379	Base & 0.918 & 0.794 & 0.682 & 0.730 & 0.595 \\
380	Instruct & 0.965 & 0.874 & 0.771 & 0.716 & 0.618 \\
381	\bottomrule
382	\end{tabular}
383	\end{table}
384	
385	The base model exhibits non-monotonic decay with a U-shaped recovery at $d_{3\text{v}4}$, while the instruction-tuned variant shows strictly monotonic decay. Both variants exceed chance (AUC $> 0.5$) at all boundaries, confirming depth signal exists regardless of instruction-tuning, though instruction-tuning strengthens and regularizes it.
386	
387	\paragraph{Caveats.}
388	For Qwen2.5-7B, the CI lower bound (58.0\%) does not exclude sub-60\% accuracy; Llama-3.1-8B's lower bound (68.3\%) is more comfortably above chance but still below the 75--83\% range at 1--1.5B.
389	The divergent AUC trajectories across two models caution against strong generalizations from only two 7--8B data points: both the monotonic (Llama-3.1) and non-monotonic (Qwen2.5) patterns are single observations, and further architectures are needed to establish which is the dominant regime at this scale.
390	
391	\paragraph{Confounds.}
392	\label{app:cross_scale_confounds}
393	Four confounds limit these results: (1)~4-bit NF4 QLoRA quantization (absent at 1--1.5B) may distort the perplexity distribution independently of depth; (2)~smaller sample size (500 vs.\ 5{,}000 per depth) widens confidence intervals; (3)~evaluation is limited to nucleus sampling, leaving other strategies untested at this scale; (4)~vocabulary mismatch between 7--8B generators and the 1.4B reference model.
394	The base-model control partially addresses a former confound (instruction-tuning): since the base variant shows weaker signal with non-monotonic decay while the instruction-tuned variant shows stronger monotonic signal, instruction-tuning regularizes rather than confounds depth estimation.
395	The remaining confounds are not mutually independent---quantization and vocabulary mismatch both affect the perplexity distribution---making it infeasible to attribute the observed accuracy gap (60--70\% vs.\ 78--85\% at 1--1.5B) to any single factor.
396	
397	\subsection{Cross-Boundary Generalization}
398	\label{app:cross_boundary}
399	
400	The preceding experiments assume a single model family generates all recursive depths.
401	In practice, recursive contamination may traverse model boundaries: text generated by model~A is used to train model~B, whose output trains model~C.
402	We probe whether the depth signal persists under two relaxations of the single-model assumption.
403	
404	\paragraph{Cross-model recursive chains.}
405	We construct a heterogeneous chain: human text (d0) $\to$ Pythia-1.4B generates d1 $\to$ OLMo-1B finetuned on Pythia-d1 generates d2 $\to$ GPT-2~XL finetuned on OLMo-d2 generates d3.
406	Each recursive step uses a \emph{different} model family, eliminating the possibility that depth signal arises from a single model's idiosyncratic behavior.
407	A 4-class Random Forest achieves 84.75\% accuracy (95\% CI $[81.0, 88.25]$), with per-depth F1 scores of 0.98 (d0), 0.88 (d1), 0.76 (d2), and 0.76 (d3).
408	Pairwise AUC remains high: d0-vs-d1 = 0.999 and d2-vs-d3 = 0.841.
409	These results suggest that distributional artifacts of recursive generation persist across model boundaries---providing preliminary evidence consistent with a process-level depth signal rather than individual generator artifacts.
410	
411	\paragraph{Confound discussion.}
412	The heterogeneous chain confounds architecture identity with depth (d1=Pythia, d2=OLMo, d3=GPT-2~XL).
413	However, if the classifier exploited architecture fingerprints rather than depth signal, near-perfect accuracy would be expected since architecture perfectly determines depth label.
414	The observed 84.75\% with monotonically decreasing per-depth F1 (d0=0.98, d1=0.88, d2=0.76, d3=0.76) is more consistent with a depth-signal interpretation, as architecture fingerprinting would not produce this graded pattern.
415	We address this confound directly with a reverse-chain control below.
416	
417	\paragraph{Reverse-chain control.}
418	To empirically test the architecture confound hypothesis, we constructed a reverse chain (GPT-2~XL $\to$ OLMo $\to$ Pythia) reversing the model-depth assignment.
419	The reverse chain achieves 85.75\% (95\% CI [82.0, 89.25]), statistically indistinguishable from the forward chain (84.75\%, [81.0, 88.25]).
420	If the classifier exploited architecture fingerprints rather than depth signal, reversing the chain should invert depth predictions; the equivalent accuracy under both orderings provides empirical evidence against the architecture confound.
421	
422	\paragraph{Cross-domain transfer.}
423	All prior experiments use WikiText-103 as the seed corpus.
424	To test domain dependence, we repeat the pipeline with arXiv abstracts as the seed text (Pythia-1.4B, nucleus $p{=}0.95$, 500 samples per depth, d0--d3).
425	Five-fold cross-validation yields 74.1\% $\pm$ 2.0\% accuracy, compared to ${\sim}$78\% on the WikiText seed.
426	Per-depth F1 shows the familiar pattern: d0 = 1.00, d1 = 0.78, d2 = 0.52, d3 = 0.66---with d2 remaining the most challenging class.
427	The 4pp accuracy gap relative to WikiText likely reflects the narrower stylistic range of scientific abstracts, which may reduce the distributional contrast between adjacent depths.
428	These results provide preliminary evidence that the perplexity-based features capture properties of the recursive generation process rather than domain-specific artifacts of the seed corpus.
429	
430	\subsection{Cross-Seed Replication}
431	\label{app:seed_replication}
432	
433	Table~\ref{tab:seed_replication} reports within-seed and cross-seed classification accuracy for Pythia-1.4B (nucleus, depths 0--3) under two independent LoRA training seeds.
434	
435	\begin{table}[h]
436	\centering
437	\small
438	\caption{Cross-seed transfer (Pythia-1.4B nucleus). Baseline seed=42 is the primary benchmark LoRA; seed=43 is an independent replication. $\Delta$: difference from respective comparison point.}
439	\label{tab:seed_replication}
440	\begin{tabular}{@{}lcc@{}}
441	\toprule
442	Condition & Acc (\%) & $\Delta$ (pp) \\
443	\midrule
444	Within-seed (seed=42) & 78.20 & --- \\
445	Within-seed (seed=43) & 77.15 & $-$1.05$^\dagger$ \\
446	\midrule
447	Cross-seed (train 42$\to$test 43) & 77.85 & \\
448	Cross-seed (train 43$\to$test 42) & 75.68 & \\
449	Cross-seed avg & 76.76 & $-$1.30$^\ddagger$ \\
450	\bottomrule
451	\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\footnotesize $^\dagger$vs.\ baseline (78.20\%). $^\ddagger$vs.\ within-seed avg (78.07\%).}
452	\end{tabular}
453	\end{table}
454	
455	The seed=43 LoRA achieves 77.15\% (95\% CI [76.4, 78.15]), within 1.05\,pp of the seed=42 baseline.
456	Cross-seed transfer averages 76.76\%, a 1.30\,pp deficit relative to within-seed performance.
457	Top-5 feature importance is identical across seeds (\texttt{var\_surprisal}, \texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{mean\_ppl}, \texttt{var\_ppl}, \texttt{p75\_ppl}), confirming that depth signal arises from the recursive process itself rather than idiosyncratic LoRA weight configurations.
458	
459	\subsection{Generation Length Ablation}
460	\label{app:length_ablation}
461	
462	Table~\ref{tab:length_ablation} reports classification accuracy as a function of passage length (Pythia-1.4B nucleus, depths 0--3).
463	
464	\begin{table}[h]
465	\centering
466	\small
467	\caption{Generation length ablation (Pythia-1.4B nucleus, 5-fold CV). Accuracy increases monotonically with passage length; the 9.47\,pp spread confirms that longer passages provide stronger statistical signal.}
468	\label{tab:length_ablation}
469	\begin{tabular}{@{}lc@{}}
470	\toprule
471	Passage length (tokens) & Acc (\%) \\
472	\midrule
473	128 & 68.35 \\
474	256 & 73.80 \\
475	512 & 77.82 \\
476	\bottomrule
477	\end{tabular}
478	\end{table}
479	
480	Depth signal is detectable from 128 tokens (2.7$\times$ chance) and saturates near 500 tokens.
481	The monotonic increase reflects the statistical nature of the features: longer passages yield more stable estimates of perplexity percentiles and surprisal variance, reducing within-class overlap at adjacent depth boundaries.
482	
483	\subsection{Mixed-Depth Corpus}
484	\label{app:mixed_depth}
485	
486	Per-passage classification is largely independent of corpus composition: evaluating on a corpus containing mixed proportions of d0--d3 passages (rather than balanced classes) yields macro-recall $\Delta{=}{-}1.62$\,pp relative to the balanced benchmark (within the 2\,pp tolerance).
487	Individual class deltas range from $-$0.45\,pp to $-$2.43\,pp (d1 shows the largest shift), confirming that the RF classifier operates on per-sample features without sensitivity to the class distribution of the evaluation corpus.
488	
489	\subsection{Extended Discussion}
490	\label{app:extended_discussion}
491	
492	\paragraph{Depth-graduated curation.}
493	Current data curation operates on a binary human-vs-machine distinction \cite{dsir2023,qurating2024}.
494	Recursive generation depth estimation enables a finer-grained alternative: retain low-depth generations (d1) whose distributional properties remain close to the human source, while down-weighting or filtering high-depth text (d3+) where tail erosion has degraded quality.
495	The 70--85\% in-distribution accuracy and $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.75}{=}4$ suggest depth-graduated filtering is feasible within known model--strategy configurations, though the d1/d2 boundary inversion under cross-strategy transfer (\S\ref{sec:gen:crossstrategy}) means reliable curation requires either known decoding strategy metadata or an upstream strategy-identification step; a pilot study (Appendix~\ref{app:curation_poc}) yields an inconclusive RF-vs-unfiltered comparison ($p>0.4$), though RF-filtered subsets significantly outperform size-matched random subsampling ($p<0.001$--$0.02$); large-scale validation remains open.
496	Importance weighting \cite{sugiyama2007_importance_weighting} could further enable continuous depth-aware data selection rather than discrete thresholding.
497	
498	\paragraph{Toward a provenance toolkit.}
499	Depth estimation complements existing provenance methods along orthogonal axes.
500	Watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark} provides high-confidence attribution when the generator cooperates but is inapplicable to unwatermarked text.
501	Source attribution \cite{uchendu2020_attribution} identifies the generating model but not the generation history.
502	Depth estimation characterizes \emph{iterative reuse} regardless of generator cooperation or identity.
503	A layered provenance system combining these three signals---watermark presence, source model, and recursive generation depth---could support more nuanced data auditing than any single method.
504

Starting with February 2025, ARR reviewers are asked to provide three scores: soundness, excitement, and overall recommendation.

## Soundness Scoring Scale (1-5)

The soundness scale includes: 5 = Excellent (this study is one of the most thorough), 4 = Strong (provides sufficient support for all claims), and 3 = Acceptable (provides sufficient support for main claims). The soundness scores must be justified by the text of the review.

## Excitement Scoring Scale (1-5)

The excitement scale includes: 5 = Highly Exciting (would recommend to others and/or attend presentation), 4 = Exciting (would mention to others and/or attend presentation), and 1 = Not Exciting (paper does not resonate and wouldn't with the *ACL community).

Excitement is subjective and doesn't necessarily follow what's popular; reviewers may perceive papers as transformational/innovative/surprising due to conceptual breakthroughs or evidence challenging assumptions, or be excited about potential impact on communities through lowering barriers or enabling new applications.

## Important Notes

Excitement scores reflect personal taste and don't necessarily come with explicit reasons. All papers recommended for Findings and main conferences are expected to be sufficiently sound and reproducible, but a paper can be worthy of the main conference even if the reviewer is not personally excited about it.

Now I have all the paper content. Let me also fetch the ARR review form page to get the exact scoring rubric, and check the specific issues mentioned in the task.

Let me now review the paper systematically against the historical issues. Let me trace through each one:

**R1-N2**: Table 2/4/5 仍无 std/CI/significance test。Figure 4 有 bootstrap CI 说明有计算能力但未推广。

Looking at the tables:
- Table 2 (tab:main_matrix): Reports accuracy percentages without std/CI


- Table 4 (tab:edd_sensitivity): Just counts of cells, no variance measures needed
- Table 5 (tab:baselines): Reports accuracy without std/CI
- Figure 4 (fig:auc_decay): Has "Shaded bands: bootstrap 95% CIs"

So the paper does have the capability to compute confidence intervals as shown in Figure 4, but hasn't applied this to the main results tables. Let me verify the exact table numbering in the document to make sure I'm mapping them correctly.

Looking at the main tables, Table 2 and Table 5 both lack standard deviations or confidence intervals. Table 5 does include a $\Delta_{\max}$ column that shows per-cell variation is at most 0.4 percentage points, which gives some sense of spread but isn't a formal uncertainty measure. The appendix does better—the cross-scale results include 95% CIs, the seed replication study reports 95% CIs, and the curation proof-of-concept table shows standard deviations with p-values. So this concern is only partially addressed in the main text, rating it as C.

Now looking at the second reviewer's point about d0 inflation—CIs are used inconsistently across tables like the cross-scale and EDD figure, but not systematically throughout all performance tables. The d0 inflation issue itself appears to be addressed: Table 2 now includes d1-d3 three-class accuracy in parentheses, and the main text explicitly discusses this in the Limitations section, noting that depth 0 achieves over 98% recall across all settings, which inflates the overall accuracy numbers. The cross-model transfer table (Table 6) is also relevant here.

For the d2 recall difficulty, the text states that d2 consistently shows the lowest recall at 46-73% across different cells, and the abstract mentions d1-d3 balanced accuracy at 55.4%, which is 1.7× chance level. So this concern seems resolved.

The fourth reviewer's note about the EDD₀.₇₅=4 statistic in the abstract is more problematic—the significance only holds for Pythia at p=0.001, while OLMo is marginal at p=0.091 and GPT-2 XL is non-significant at p=0.505. The phrase "consistent direction" in the abstract may be overstating the evidence given these mixed results. ), $p = 0.091$ for OLMo (marginal), and $p = 0.505$ for GPT-2 XL (non-significant). So the pattern holds across all three model families, but the statistical evidence weakens considerably—Pythia shows strong significance while the other two are much less convincing. The abstract's phrasing of "consistent direction across all three families with graded statistical support" does capture this stratification, though it's a somewhat gentle way of describing how GPT-2 XL essentially shows no significant effect. Still, by explicitly noting that the strongest claim applies specifically to Pythia, the abstract appropriately constrains the scope of what's being claimed.

For the Related Work section, I'm noticing some key citations are missing. Schaeffer et al. 2025 directly challenges benchmark ecological validity but isn't cited. The ordinal classification foundations—McCullagh 1980 and Rennie & Srebro 2005—aren't referenced either, even though the paper discusses ordinal regression methods. CCNet from Wenzek et al. 2020 is also absent. I should verify this against the references file to be sure, but from what I can see in the Related Work text, these gaps appear to be unaddressed.

For the LoRA rank sensitivity analysis, the method section only specifies r=16 with α=32, and the cross-seed replication uses the same configuration. There's no exploration of how performance varies across different ranks like {4, 16, 64}, so this ablation study is missing.

On the reference model circularity issue, the Limitations section does acknowledge that Pythia serves as both generator and reference, creating a potential dependency problem. The paper suggests adding an architecturally distinct reference model as an ablation, but this hasn't been implemented yet. The single LoRA instance concern is actually addressed—they ran independent replications with different seeds and showed the depth signal persists across them, confirming it's not an artifact of specific weights. For the EDD classifier-dependence issue, the definition explicitly specifies the Random Forest configuration, but there's no explicit statement acknowledging that EDD is fundamentally an operational measure tied to that classifier choice—it's more implicit in how they present it.

Looking at their comparison across different classifiers in Table 5, the spread is minimal (≤0.4pp), which indirectly suggests EDD isn't highly sensitive to classifier choice, but they never directly state this as a limitation or design decision. So this is partially addressed through empirical evidence rather than explicit methodological declaration.

The accumulation scenario—where a training corpus mixes different recursion depths (like 70% d0 and 30% d1)—isn't tested anywhere in the paper. They discuss mixed-depth evaluation sets in the appendix, but that's about class imbalance during testing, not about the corpus itself being a mixture of generations. This gap remains unaddressed.

Now considering whether depth estimation is just quality estimation in disguise. The paper would need matched-quality controls—taking texts of similar quality at different depths and showing they're still distinguishable. The temperature robustness analysis hints at this (the signal collapses when memorization doesn't occur), and the cross-model chains suggest it's about the generation process rather than a single model's quality gradient. But there's no explicit matched-quality control experiment, so while there's indirect evidence, it's not directly addressed.

Looking at presentation issues now: the abstract is quite dense at 10 lines with many numbers packed in. There's also a minor inconsistency where the abstract claims "70–85% four-class accuracy" but Table 2 shows 69.6% to 85.4%—the lower bound should either be stated as 69.6% or rounded consistently. And the EDD_{0.75}=4 claim in the abstract doesn't quite match what I'm seeing in the depth 0-3 grid at that temperature.

The cross-model transfer results are honestly reported with moderate balanced accuracy of 55.4% (1.7× chance baseline), and the curation proof-of-concept shows that RF-filtered versus unfiltered results aren't statistically significant. However, the main tables lack error bars or confidence intervals—only some appendix tables include them, which is a notable gap for a methods paper.

I'm also noticing some methodological concerns: the paper uses the same reference model (Pythia-1.4B) for both feature extraction and as a generator, though the Limitations section does address this by showing GPT-2 XL achieves higher accuracy despite being cross-model. The BOS-seeded generation without prompt conditioning is acknowledged as potentially amplifying the depth signal, but it limits real-world applicability. The 512-token passage length is also quite long for practical use—the 128-token result shows significant performance degradation to 68.35%.

Now I should verify the references before writing up my full review.

Good, I now have all the information I need. Let me also fetch the actual review form page to get the complete scoring rubric. But actually, I have enough to proceed with the review. Let me compile my findings.

Let me now write the comprehensive review. Let me verify the references for the missing citations:

1. **Schaeffer et al. 2025** - Not in references.bib. Looking at the bib entries, there's `gerstgrasser2024_accumulate` which has Schaeffer as a co-author, but this is Gerstgrasser et al. 

2024. There's no standalone Schaeffer et al. 2025 about benchmark ecological validity.

2. **McCullagh 1980** (proportional odds model) - Not in references.bib. The ordinal classification section only cites CORAL (2020) and CLOC (2025).

3. **Rennie & Srebro 2005** - Not in references.bib.

4. **CCNet (Wenzek et al. 2020)** - Not in references.bib.

So R5-W4 is clearly not addressed. Now I'm checking internal consistency claims, starting with what the abstract claims about the four-class performance metrics.

The abstract states 70-85% accuracy, and Table 2 shows 69.6% to 85.4%, so the lower bound is just a rounding up of 69.6%. The cross-model transfer claim of 66.4% with d1-d3 balanced accuracy at 55.4% and 1.7× chance checks out against Table 6 and the calculation (49.9+59.2+57.2)/3 = 55.4%, which gives 1.66× rounded to 1.7×. The bidirectional recursive chain numbers of 84.75% and 85.75% are confirmed in the appendix. I'm now verifying the preliminary cross-scale claims.

For the EDD_{0.75}=4 threshold, I'm checking the AUC values across models: Pythia shows d3-vs-d4 at 0.784 and d4-vs-d5 at 0.683, confirming EDD=4 at the 0.75 threshold with p=0.001. OLMo's d3-vs-d4 is 0.765 (p=0.091), and GPT-2 XL hits exactly 0.750 at d3-vs-d4 (p=0.505), so the threshold claim holds across the models tested.

Now I'm verifying the introduction's claim about perplexity tail statistics being top-2 features in 9/9 and 8/9 configurations—Table 3 shows p90_ppl is indeed bolded as a top-2 feature across the configurations.

Let me organize the key findings for the review, starting with the historical issues status.

Looking at how the authors addressed previous reviewer concerns: the confidence intervals issue is only partially resolved since they appear in some tables but not the main ones; the d0 inflation problem is fixed with accuracy breakdowns now shown; the EDD statistical qualification got some attention in the abstract though the language remains somewhat vague; the related work still has notable gaps with several important papers missing; LoRA rank sensitivity wasn't addressed at all; and the reference model circularity concern received partial treatment in the discussion.

Beyond what was already covered, I'm noticing that the cross-seed replication work resolved the LoRA non-independence issue, but there are still unresolved problems: the classifier-dependence of EDD is only partially addressed since convergence is shown but not explicitly declared; the partial mixing and accumulation concerns weren't tackled; and quality estimation repackaging wasn't addressed either. The most glaring gap is that the main result tables still lack variance estimates despite the paper showing it can compute confidence intervals elsewhere—this is a fundamental issue for an empirical contribution. There's also the matter of the abstract's "70-85%" claim needing more precision.

## Round 8 审稿报告 — Reviewer 1（方法严谨性 + 实验有效性）

**论文**: How Deep Is Your Data? Estimating Recursive Generation Depth via Statistical Fingerprints
**Venue**: EMNLP 2026 Findings (ARR May 2026 cycle)

---

## 总体评分

**Overall Recommendation**: 3.0 (Resubmit next cycle — needs targeted revisions achievable in one cycle)
**一句话总结**: 核心方法新颖且实验覆盖面宽，但主表格缺统计不确定性度量、EDD 跨模型统计支撑不均、以及 accumulation/quality-control 实验缺失等问题需在 camera-ready 前解决。

---

## 官方维度打分（ACL ARR Review Form, Feb 2025+）

| 维度 | 分数 | 理由摘要 |
|------|------|----------|
| Soundness | 3/5 (Acceptable) | 主 claims 有支撑但 key tables 缺 CI/significance；EDD=4 的跨模型泛化声明统计基础不均（1/3 显著） |
| Excitement | 3.5/5 | 问题定义新颖（ordinal depth estimation 是真空白），atlas 设计系统性好，但实用性论证（curation PoC p=0.407）偏弱 |
| Reproducibility | 4/5 | Pipeline 描述清晰（LoRA hyperparams, feature extraction, CV splits），承诺代码公开；cross-seed replication 加分 |
| Clarity | 4/5 | 结构清晰，limitations 诚实透明；abstract 偏长且数字密集 |

---

## 历史遗留 Issue 逐条验证

### ✅ RESOLVED

**R1-W2** (d0 inflation): Table 2 现在括号内报告 d1-d3 三类 accuracy（chance=33%），Limitations 段明确讨论 d0 inflation，Abstract 也报告 "d1-d3 balanced accuracy: 55.4%, 1.7× chance"。

**R5-W1** (Single LoRA non-independence): Appendix §A.10 提供 cross-seed replication（seed=43, Δ=-1.05pp, 95% CI [76.4, 78.15]）和 cross-seed transfer（76.76%），top-5 feature importance 跨 seed 一致。充分证明 depth signal 不是特定 LoRA 权重的 artifact。

### ⚠️ PARTIALLY ADDRESSED

**R1-N2** (Tables 缺 std/CI/significance):
- Figure 4 有 bootstrap 95% CI shaded bands ✓
- Cross-scale Table (Appendix §A.7) 有 95% CI brackets ✓
- Cross-seed Table (Appendix §A.10) 有 95% CI ✓
- **但 Table 2（核心 9-cell matrix）和 Table 5（classifier comparison）仍无任何 variance 指标**。Table 5 有 Δ_max 列（≤0.4pp）替代，但这不等于正式的 CI 或 std。5-fold CV 天然产生 fold-level variance，不报告是遗憾。
- 状态：主文核心表格仍缺，附录/图中有。建议至少在 Table 2 加 ±std 或 95% CI。

**R4-N1** (EDD₀.₇₅=4 统计限定):
- Abstract 现在写 "for the best-characterized model family (Pythia, p=0.001; consistent direction across all three families with graded statistical support; §4.4)" ✓ 范围已限定到 Pythia
- §4.4 正文完整报告三个 p-values：Pythia 0.001, OLMo 0.091, GPT-2 XL 0.505 ✓
- 问题：Abstract 中 "consistent direction... with graded statistical support" 仍是 euphemism——GPT-2 XL p=0.505 意味着其 AUC 点估计 0.750 完全无法排除随机波动（H₀: AUC≤0.75 无法拒绝）。"Graded statistical support" 在统计学中无标准含义，可能误导读者以为三个模型都显示了有意义的证据。建议改为 "Pythia significant (p=0.001), OLMo marginal (p=0.091), GPT-2 XL non-significant" 的精确表述，或至少在 abstract 内明示仅 Pythia 具备充分统计支撑。

**R5-N2** (Reference model 循环依赖):
- Limitations 段充分讨论了 self-model 测量问题 ✓
- OLMo-1B 作为 alternative reference 的 ablation（Δ=4.0pp）存在 ✓
- 明确指出 "architecturally distinct references (e.g., encoder-only or larger-scale models) remains open" ✓
- 但建议的 architecturally distinct reference ablation 未执行。考虑到两个 reference 都是 ~1B autoregressive models，无法排除这一架构族系的 bias。

**R5-W5** (EDD classifier-dependence):
- §5.1 Table 5 展示 RF/XGBoost/LightGBM 在同一特征上的 convergence（Δ≤0.4pp）✓ 间接表明 EDD 对 classifier 不敏感
- 但 EDD 定义（Definition 1）仍未显式声明 "EDD is an operational measure conditioned on the specified classifier and feature set"。当前写法可能让读者误以为 EDD 是 text 的 intrinsic property。建议在 Definition 1 后加一句 methodological caveat。

### ❌ NOT ADDRESSED

**R5-W4** (Related Work 引用遗漏):
- **McCullagh 1980** (proportional odds model): ordinal classification 的奠基论文，当前 §2 "Ordinal Classification" 段只引 CORAL (2020) 和 CLOC (2025)，缺少经典基础。
- **Rennie & Srebro 2005** (loss design for ordinal regression): 同上。
- **CCNet / Wenzek et al. 2020**: 未引。CCNet 是 Common Crawl 数据清洗 pipeline，与本文讨论的 web-crawl calibration（C4）高度相关。
- **Schaeffer et al. 2025**: 直接挑战 benchmark ecological validity 的论文未引（注意 Gerstgrasser et al. 2024 中 Schaeffer 是共同作者，但那是不同论文）。
- 状态：references.bib 中无上述四项。建议至少补充 McCullagh 和 Schaeffer。

**R1-W3** (LoRA rank sensitivity analysis):
- 论文始终使用 r=16, α=32。Cross-seed replication（§A.10）使用相同 rank。
- 未报告 rank ∈ {4, 16, 64} 的 sensitivity analysis。
- 这是重要的方法学缺失：如果 depth signal 因 rank 改变而显著变化，则当前结论的适用范围受限。至少需要一组 rank ablation 数据。

**R7-W3** (Partial mixing/accumulation 场景):
- Limitations 提到 "wild recursive contamination, where models are pretrained on mixed corpora containing prior-generation outputs at unknown proportions" 并承认 "fingerprints we identify may attenuate or shift under such diffuse exposure"。
- Appendix §A.9 (Mixed-Depth Corpus) 测试的是 evaluation set 中 class 比例变化对分类器的影响（macro-recall Δ=-1.62pp），**不是**训练数据本身为混合深度的情况。
- 真正的 accumulation 场景（如 Gerstgrasser et al. 2024 的 accumulate 设定：训练集 = 70% d0 + 30% d1，从此混合数据 finetune 后生成）完全未测试。这是 ecological validity 的核心缺口。

**R7-W4** (Depth estimation vs. text quality estimation):
- 无 matched-quality control 实验。论文未测试：在控制 text quality（如 perplexity level、coherence score）的条件下，depth 是否仍可区分。
- 间接证据存在：τ=1.1 时 signal 消失说明不纯粹是 quality；cross-model chains 排除了单一模型的 quality gradient。但缺少直接的 confound-control 实验。
- 这是一个 conceptual concern：如果 depth 与 quality 强相关且无法解耦，则 "depth estimation" 可能只是 "quality estimation" 的重包装。

---

## 新发现问题

### Must-Fix（影响接收决定）

**N1** [critical] Abstract 数值精度问题
- 位置：Abstract line 1-2, §1
- 问题：Abstract 写 "70--85% four-class accuracy"，但 Table 2 实际范围为 69.6%--85.4%。下界 69.6% 被向上取整至 70%。虽然差异仅 0.4pp，但在 blind review 中审稿人可能质疑数据 cherry-picking。
- 建议：改为 "approximately 70--85%" 或 "69.6--85.4%"。

**N2** [critical] Curation PoC 与 narrative 不一致
- 位置：§6 Discussion, Appendix §A.6
- 问题：Discussion 将 depth-graduated curation 作为核心 motivation 之一，但 Appendix Table 9 显示 RF-filtered vs. unfiltered 无统计显著差异（p=0.407, 0.492, 0.607）。仅 RF vs. random subsampling 显著（p<0.001--0.02）。这意味着 depth-aware filtering 相比 simply keeping all data 无可证明的益处——只是优于随机丢弃数据。
- 为什么影响接收：核心 application narrative（"enables depth-graduated data curation"）缺乏实验支撑。如果 curation 是 motivation 之一，inconclusive 结果需要在主文而非仅附录中诚实呈现。
- 建议：(1) 在 Discussion 中明确说明 curation PoC 目前 inconclusive，或 (2) 降低 narrative 中对 curation 的强调，将其定位为 future work 而非 established benefit。

### Should-Fix（影响评分）

**W1** [warning] EDD 在 GPT-2 XL 上的 boundary case
- 位置：§4.4, Abstract
- 问题：GPT-2 XL d3-vs-d4 AUC = 0.750，恰好等于 threshold T=0.75。定义上 EDD≥4（因为 ≥），但 bootstrap test p=0.505 说明这个点估计完全无法区分于 random fluctuation。论文将此纳入 "consistent direction" 表述中，但数学上 AUC=0.750 at T=0.75 with p=0.505 是一个 null result。
- 建议：在 §4.4 中明确指出 GPT-2 XL 的 EDD=4 结论在统计上是 trivial 的（AUC 恰好等于阈值且无显著性），避免读者误解三个模型都 robustly 支持 EDD=4。

**W2** [warning] Cross-strategy transfer failure 与 "universal fingerprint" narrative 的张力
- 位置：§5.3, §1（Introduction "universal and scale-variant"）
- 问题：Introduction 声称 fingerprints 是 "universal and scale-variant"，但 cross-strategy transfer（§5.3）仅 59.1% mean accuracy，d1-d3 仅 45.9%（chance=33%，1.38×），temperature holdout d1v2 AUC 可低至 0.129（GPT-2 XL）。这不是 "universal" 的表现——strategy-conditioned classifiers 是必需的。
- 建议：将 Introduction 的 "universal" 修饰为 "universal within-strategy" 或限定 universality 的范围。当前措辞对读者产生过度乐观的印象。

**W3** [warning] 95% CI 未报告在 primary result tables
- 位置：Table 2, Table 5
- 问题：5-fold CV 本身产生 5 个 fold-level accuracy，可直接报告 mean±std。Table 2 和 Table 5 是论文最核心的 result tables，却是唯二没有 variance measure 的主要表格。Figure 4 有 bootstrap CI，cross-scale table 有 95% CI——说明作者有计算能力但选择性地省略了。
- 建议：Table 2 加 ±std 列（或 95% CI），Table 5 的 Δ_max 列改为标准 std 报告。

### Minor（不影响接收）

- Abstract 过度压缩（~250 words，数字密集），建议删减 cross-model chain 的具体百分比（84.75%/85.75%）以提高可读性。
- §3.4 EDD 定义的 footnote 1 解释了 non-monotonic 情况，但正文未在 Definition 后 explicitly state "EDD is defined relative to the classifier and feature set specified above"。
- Table 2 caption 说 "Depth-0 recall exceeds 98% in all cells" 但 Table 8 (Appendix) 显示 GPT-2 XL top-k 为 98.5%——consistent，只是 "exceeds 98%" 与 98.5% 的 margin 很小。
- §1 "our key insight is that recursive generation leaves quantifiable statistical fingerprints... universal and scale-variant"：前半句是 post-hoc conclusion 而非 a priori insight；建议改为 hypothesis-driven 表述。

---

## 主要优势

1. **问题新颖性**：Ordinal depth estimation 确实是文献空白。从 binary detection 到 ordinal classification 的推进有明确的科学价值。
2. **系统性实验设计**：3×3 atlas 设计优雅，覆盖了 model family 和 decoding strategy 两个维度的交叉效应。
3. **诚实的 Limitations**：8 段 Limitations 覆盖了大部分可预见的批评，这在 submission 中罕见。Cross-seed replication、domain bias analysis、base-model control 都体现了方法学严谨性。
4. **特征可解释性**：p90_ppl + var_surprisal 作为 dominant features 的一致性（9/9 + 8/9，三种 importance measures concordance W=0.90）令人信服。
5. **Ablation 充分性**：feature ablation、classifier convergence、passage length、reference model、cross-seed——覆盖面广。

---

## 总结判断

论文定义了一个有价值的新任务，实验覆盖系统性好，但三个核心方法学问题阻碍接收：(1) 主表格缺 CI 降低了 reproducibility claim 的可信度；(2) EDD=4 的跨模型泛化统计支撑不均匀且 abstract 表述 euphemistic；(3) accumulation 场景和 matched-quality control 两个关键生态效度实验完全缺失。这些问题中 (1)(2) 可在一个 cycle 内修复，(3) 需要额外实验但技术上可行。建议 resubmit next cycle。

**Confidence**: 4/5 (I am confident but not certain about my assessment)

## Round 8 交叉回应 — Reviewer 1 对 Reviewer 2 审稿意见

---

### Must-Fix 逐条回应

**[AGREE] R2-N1: Related Work 遗漏 Schaeffer et al. 2025**

同意。我在独立审稿中也将此标记为 R5-W4 未解决项。Schaeffer et al. 2025 ("Position: Model Collapse Does Not Mean What You Think") 直接质疑 model collapse 在实际混合数据条件下的必然性，而本文 Introduction §1 第一段以 "a recursive loop emerges... it is already occurring in the wild" 作为核心前提。不引用并回应最直接的反对声音是 Related Work 的显著缺陷。

补充：Gerstgrasser et al. 2024（已在 references.bib 中，Schaeffer 为共同作者）讨论了 accumulation 设定下 collapse 可避免，但那是一篇独立的论文，不能替代 Schaeffer et al. 2025 的 position paper 所提出的更根本的质疑。

---

**[AGREE] R2-N2: 核心发现增量贡献定位不清**

部分同意，但认为严重程度应从 critical 降为 should-fix。

理由：
- R2 正确指出 "perplexity tail statistics dominate depth discrimination" 本质上是 Dohmatob 2024 tail-erosion theory 的 empirical consequence。如果论文仅发现此点，novelty 确实不足。
- 但论文的实际增量不仅在于 feature-level observation，还包括：(1) task formalization as ordinal classification (§3.1)；(2) EDD metric + contiguous discriminability 概念 (§3.4)；(3) strategy-dependent trajectory 差异——temperature accelerates convergence, top-k attenuates signal (§4.5)——这些是 Dohmatob 理论未预测的 empirical findings；(4) benchmark construction enabling future work。
- **但 R2 的建议完全正确**：论文应在 Introduction 中明确 position 自己为 "theory → practice bridge"，承认 feature-level finding 的 theoretical prior（Dohmatob），并将 novelty claim 集中在 strategy-dependent dynamics、EDD formalization 和 cross-model generalization 上。当前写法（§1 "Our key insight is that recursive generation leaves quantifiable statistical fingerprints"）暗示这是全新发现，但 Dohmatob 2024 已经从理论上预测了这一点。

建议：将 critical 改为 should-fix，因为增量贡献存在但 positioning 需调整。

---

**[AGREE] R2-N3: Abstract §4.4 引用 + 数字过载**

完全同意。我在审稿 Minor 中也注意到 abstract 数字密集。

具体问题：
1. "§4.4" 出现在 Abstract (abstract.tex line 6) 是明确的 format violation——Abstract 必须是自包含阅读单元。
2. 我计数 Abstract 中的数值：180K, 3, 3, 4, 19, 70--85%, 25%, 9/9, 8/9, EDD₀.₇₅=4, p=0.001, 66.4%, 55.4%, 1.7×, 84.75%, 85.75%, 70.2%, EDD=4, 60.1%, 59.9%, 70.2%, 98.5%... 超过 20 个数字。这远超正常 NLP 论文 abstract 密度。
3. 审稿人在 30 秒内无法从这种密度中提取核心 message。

但我将此标为 should-fix 而非 critical——这是写作质量问题而非方法学缺陷，不应单独影响接收决定。技术内容有效前提下，abstract 可以在 camera-ready 时修订。

---

### Should-Fix 逐条回应

**[AGREE] R2-W1: "universal and scale-variant" 矛盾措辞**

完全同意。我在独立审稿中也标记了此问题（我的 W2）。Introduction §1 写 fingerprints are "universal and scale-variant"，但 cross-strategy transfer 仅 59.1%（d1-d3: 45.9%, 1.38× chance），temperature holdout d1v2 AUC 低至 0.129 (§5.3 GPT-2 XL)。Strategy-conditioned classifiers 是必需的——这不是 "universal" 的定义。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W2: Discussion "enables" vs PoC "inconclusive" 张力**

完全同意。我在独立审稿中将此标为 N2 (critical)。Discussion §6 写 "Depth estimation enables depth-graduated data curation"，但 Appendix Table 9 显示 RF-filtered vs. unfiltered p=0.407/0.492/0.607——全部 non-significant。仅 RF vs. random subsampling 显著。论文主文不应用 "enables" 描述一个 inconclusive 的 PoC。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W3: "signal universality" overclaim**

同意。generalization.tex 最后一句 (line 110): "Cross-model recursive chains (84.75%)... further confirm signal universality." 但：
- Cross-strategy transfer 仅 59.1%（§5.3）
- Cross-τ transfer 仅 46.7%（Appendix §A.4）
- Cross-model transfer d2 recall 低至 26.8%（Table 6, Pythia holdout）

"Signal universality" 在这些数据下是 overclaim。更准确的描述是 "signal persists across model boundaries under matched strategy conditions"。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W4: Contribution bullet 3 信息过载**

同意。Introduction contribution list 第三条（introduction.tex lines 28-29）在一个 bullet 中堆砌了 7 个数字和 5 个 generalization axes，读起来像 results summary 而非 contribution statement。Contribution bullets 应陈述 what was achieved，具体数字放在相应 section。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W5: 遗漏 CCNet (Wenzek et al. 2020)**

同意。我在独立审稿中也标记了此遗漏。CCNet 是 perplexity-based web data filtering 的 foundational work，与本文使用 perplexity features 进行 depth-based filtering 有直接方法论关联。Appendix §A.5 讨论 C4 calibration 时不引 CCNet 是明显缺失。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W6: Ordinal classification 引用基础薄弱**

同意。我在独立审稿中也标记了此点。McCullagh 1980 (proportional odds model) 是 ordinal regression 的奠基论文。当前 §2 Ordinal Classification 段仅引 CORAL (2020) 和 CLOC (2025)，缺少理论基础。补充 McCullagh 1980 和 Rennie & Srebro 2005 不需要额外实验，仅需 1-2 句话和 bib entries。

---

### Minor 逐条回应

**[AGREE] em-dash 和 -ing phrases**: Abstract line 1 已有 "arises---yet"，虽然技术上是 LaTeX 的三连 hyphen 生成的 em-dash，但仍是 AI 写作的典型标志。同意需要全文清理。

**[REBUT] DivEye year**: references.bib 中 DivEye 标注为 TMLR 2026（diveye2026 entry, line 206-212），arXiv ID 2509.18880 (Sep 2025 submission, 2026 publication)。R2 认为应为 2025，但 publication venue year 标注 2026 是合理的——投稿于 2025 但 published in TMLR 2026。两种标注方式都有合理性，建议作者与 TMLR 官方 publication date 对齐即可。非实质问题。

**[AGREE] conclusion.tex 命名混淆**: 文件名为 conclusion.tex 但实际包含的是 Limitations + Ethics Statement，而 Discussion and Conclusion 的内容在 discussion.tex 中。这确实容易让读者（或 collaborator）混淆。

---

### 总结

我与 R2 的 9 条 Must-Fix/Should-Fix 中有 **9/9 方向一致**，但在严重程度上有 2 处分歧：
1. R2-N2 我认为应从 critical 降为 should-fix（增量贡献存在，只是 positioning 需调整）
2. R2-N3 我认为应从 critical 降为 should-fix（写作问题非方法学缺陷）

我的独立审稿中标记的几个问题 R2 未覆盖：
- 主表格 (Table 2, 5) 缺 std/CI（我的 R1-N2 续，R2 未提及）
- LoRA rank sensitivity 缺失（我的 R1-W3 续，R2 未提及）
- Accumulation 场景未验证（我的 R7-W3 续，R2 未提及）
- Matched-quality control 缺失（我的 R7-W4 续，R2 未提及）

这些方法学问题可能比 R2 关注的 framing/positioning 问题对接收决定影响更大。

[Round 1 审稿请求]:
## Review Assignment: R1 — Method & Experiments

**Venue:** EMNLP 2026 Main (via ACL Rolling Review)
**Paper:** "Ordinal Depth Estimation for Recursive Language Model Generations: A Depth Degradation Atlas Across Scales and Strategies"

**Scoring system (ARR 2025+):** Three scores on 1–5 scale: Soundness, Excitement, Overall Assessment.
- 5 = Top ~2%, exceptional
- 4 = Strong, warrants acceptance at a top *ACL venue
- 3 = Good, could be published but may not be top-tier
- 2 = Borderline, has merit but significant flaws
- 1 = Poor, significant flaws

**Your focus:** Method soundness, experimental rigor, statistical validity, reproducibility.

### Paper Summary
The paper formalizes "ordinal generation depth estimation": predicting how many recursive generation cycles (d ∈ {0,1,2,3}) a text passage has undergone, where depth 0 is human-written. The authors:
1. Construct a 3-model × 3-strategy × 4-depth benchmark (Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, GPT-2 XL; nucleus/temperature/top-k; LoRA fine-tuning at each depth)
2. Extract 19 statistical features from a fixed reference model (Pythia-1.4B) and train RF/LR classifiers achieving 70–85% four-class accuracy (chance=25%)
3. Build a "Depth Degradation Atlas" revealing: universal depth markers (p90_ppl, var_surprisal), monotonic AUC decay, and strategy-dependent feature trajectory reversal under temperature sampling
4. Extend to 14B scale (Qwen2.5-14B, FP16, 76.2% accuracy) and prompted generation (92.8% retention vs BOS)
5. Propose a two-stage pipeline (strategy identification → conditioned depth classification) achieving 75.2%, +3.2pp over naive pooling
6. Apply classifiers to wild web data (RedPajama-v2, Dolma) showing consistent FPR gradients and temporal signal

### Evaluate These Dimensions

**A. Task Formalization (Section 3.1)**
- Is the problem definition (Eq. 1-2) clean and well-motivated?
- Is the EDD metric (Eq. 2) a meaningful contribution?

**B. Benchmark Construction (Section 3.2)**
- Is the 3×3×4 design sufficient? What's missing?
- Is LoRA-only fine-tuning a significant limitation?
- Sample sizes per configuration — are they reported clearly?

**C. Feature Extraction (Section 3.3)**
- Are 19 features well-chosen? Any obvious omissions?
- Is the fixed reference model (Pythia-1.4B) design sound?
- Is there a circularity concern when classifying Pythia-generated text?

**D. Classification (Section 3.4)**
- RF + LR only — should neural baselines be included?
- Is 5-fold stratified CV appropriate? Should there be held-out test sets?
- Are confidence intervals and significance tests adequate?

**E. Scale & Ecological Validity (Sections 5.2-5.3)**
- Does one 14B experiment suffice for "scale robustness" claims?
- Is the prompted generation experiment convincing for ecological validity?
- KS test for feature distribution comparison — appropriate?

**F. Two-Stage Pipeline (Section 5.4)**
- Is the v1→v2 improvement well-motivated?
- Oracle vs predicted gap analysis — is this analysis sound?
- Is 75.2% vs 72.0% (+3.2pp) a meaningful improvement?

**G. Wild-Data Calibration (Section 5.5)**
- Without ground-truth, how interpretable are these results?
- Is the temporal analysis (pre/post 2023) well-caveated?
- FPR estimation methodology — is it justified?

**H. Reproducibility**
- Are all hyperparameters specified?
- Is the experimental pipeline reproducible?
- Is code/data availability mentioned?

Provide: (1) numbered strengths, (2) numbered weaknesses, (3) questions for authors, (4) preliminary scores (Soundness, Excitement, Overall) with justification.

1	\section{The Depth Degradation Atlas}
2	\label{sec:atlas}
3	
4	We present the Depth Degradation Atlas: a systematic empirical map of how statistical fingerprints evolve across recursive generation depths, models, and decoding strategies.
5	The atlas spans $3 \times 3 = 9$ model--strategy cells evaluated at depths $d \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$, with depth extensions to $d{=}5$ for cross-model EDD validation (\S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}).
6	
7	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
8	\subsection{In-Distribution Performance}
9	\label{sec:atlas:id}
10	
11	Table~\ref{tab:main_matrix} reports four-class Random Forest accuracy (5-fold CV, 200 trees) across all nine cells.
12	Accuracy ranges from 69.6\% (Pythia, top-$k$) to 85.4\% (GPT-2~XL, temperature), all exceeding the 25\% chance baseline by a wide margin.
13	Two axis effects emerge.
14	GPT-2~XL achieves the highest accuracy under every strategy (76.6--85.4\%), followed by OLMo (74.2--82.0\%) and Pythia (69.6--78.2\%).
15	Top-$k$ sampling yields the lowest accuracy in every model.
16	The mean within-model strategy gap is 8.4~pp, comparable to the 7.1~pp mean within-strategy model gap; decoding strategy and model family contribute roughly equally to performance variance.
17	
18	\begin{table}[t]
19	\centering
20	\small
21	\caption{Four-class RF accuracy (\%) across the $3 \times 3$ atlas, with d1--d3 three-class accuracy in parentheses (chance = 25\% / 33\%). Depth-0 recall exceeds 98\% in all cells.}
22	\label{tab:main_matrix}
23	\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
24	\toprule
25	& Nucleus & Temp.\ $\tau{=}0.9$ & Top-$k$ \\
26	\midrule
27	Pythia-1.4B  & 78.2\,(71.2) & 76.3\,(70.6) & 69.6\,(58.8) \\
28	OLMo-1B     & 78.8\,(75.0) & 82.0\,(76.3) & 74.2\,(66.1) \\
29	GPT-2~XL    & 83.3\,(79.0) & 85.4\,(82.6) & 76.6\,(69.5) \\
30	\bottomrule
31	\end{tabular}
32	\end{table}
33	
34	\paragraph{Per-class recall distribution.}
35	Depth-0 recall exceeds 98\% in all 9 cells, confirming that human-written text is trivially separable from any generation depth.
36	Among generated depths, d2 consistently yields the lowest recall (46--73\% across cells), followed by d3 (58--82\%) and d1 (72--91\%).
37	For example, Pythia-1.4B nucleus achieves per-class recall of d0$\,{=}\,$99\%, d1$\,{=}\,$82\%, d2$\,{=}\,$59\%, d3$\,{=}\,$72\%.
38	The strongest d2 recall is obtained by GPT-2~XL nucleus (73\%).
39	The d2 trough reflects its position at the center of the depth gradient: d2 features overlap with both the d1 distribution above and d3 below, making it the most confusable class, consistent with the d2-vs-d3 pair being the EDD bottleneck (\S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}).
40	Full per-class recall for all cells appears in Appendix~\ref{app:per_class}.
41	
42	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
43	\subsection{Feature Consistency Across the Grid}
44	\label{sec:atlas:features}
45	
46	Despite the 15.8~pp accuracy spread across cells, a small feature family dominates in every setting.
47	Perplexity tail statistics as a feature group dominate depth discrimination: the 90th-percentile perplexity (\texttt{p90\_ppl}) ranks top-2 by Gini importance in all 9 cells; surprisal variance (\texttt{var\_surprisal}) in 8/9 under SHAP (7/9 under Gini; Appendix~\ref{app:permutation}).\footnote{Individual feature rankings should be interpreted cautiously given high multicollinearity (VIF${>}$10 for 14--16/19 features); the group-level dominance of perplexity tail statistics is robust across importance measures.}
48	Table~\ref{tab:feature_importance} shows the full per-cell ranking.
49	
50	Cross-model feature-rank Spearman correlation averages $\bar{\rho} = 0.868$ (range $[0.619, 0.954]$): models agree on which features carry depth information even when they differ in absolute accuracy.
51	Among strategies, top-$k$ yields the highest cross-model rank correlation ($\rho = 0.811$): the deterministic vocabulary truncation imposes a more uniform feature landscape across architectures, at the cost of weaker overall signal (\S\ref{sec:atlas:strategy}).
52	
53	Percentile-based features outperform their moment-based counterparts.
54	Token-level perplexity distributions are heavy-tailed: individual outlier passages can dominate the arithmetic mean of their depth class, whereas \texttt{p90\_ppl} is robust to such extremes while still capturing the tail erosion that signals generation depth.
55	
56	Feature ablation confirms this concentration: the top-2 features (\texttt{p90\_ppl} + \texttt{var\_surprisal}) alone reach 91.1\% of full accuracy (71.5\%), and the top-5 features achieve 97.6\% (76.5\% vs.\ 78.4\%), with perplexity statistics alone reaching 76.6\% (vs.\ surprisal 73.2\%, other categories ${\leq}$47\%).
57	Variance inflation analysis reveals VIF${>}$10 for 14--16 of 19 features, placing the effective independent dimensionality at ${\approx}$4--5.
58	Forward selection independently confirms the dominant pair: \texttt{p90\_ppl} is selected first in 6/9 cells, \texttt{var\_surprisal} in 3/9.
59	
60	The feature hierarchy also shifts with depth.
61	At shallow boundaries (d1 vs.\ d2), \texttt{var\_surprisal} dominates importance; at deeper boundaries (d3 vs.\ d4, d4 vs.\ d5), tail perplexity statistics (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{kurtosis\_ppl}) take over.
62	This transition aligns with model-collapse dynamics~\cite{shumailov2024_nature}: early recursion narrows the surprisal distribution (captured by its variance), while later steps erode the perplexity tail (captured by upper quantiles and kurtosis).
63	
64	\begin{table}[t]
65	\centering
66	\small
67	\caption{Top-5 features by Gini importance. \textbf{Bold}: top-2. \texttt{p90\_ppl} top-2 in 9/9; \texttt{var\_surprisal} 8/9 under SHAP (7/9 under Gini).}
68	\label{tab:feature_importance}
69	\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
70	\begin{tabular}{@{}l l@{}}
71	\toprule
72	Cell & Top-5 features (Gini importance, ranked) \\
73	\midrule
74	Pythia, nuc.       & \textbf{var\_surp\,(.17)}, \textbf{p90\_ppl\,(.15)}, m\_ppl\,(.11), var\_ppl\,(.08), p75\,(.07) \\
75	Pythia, $\tau$     & \textbf{var\_surp\,(.17)}, \textbf{p90\_ppl\,(.14)}, m\_ppl\,(.11), p75\,(.07), m\_surp\,(.07) \\
76	Pythia, top-$k$    & \textbf{var\_surp\,(.16)}, \textbf{p90\_ppl\,(.12)}, m\_ppl\,(.11), var\_ppl\,(.07), m\_surp\,(.06) \\
77	GPT-2\,XL, nuc.    & \textbf{var\_surp\,(.21)}, \textbf{p90\_ppl\,(.21)}, p75\,(.10), m\_surp\,(.07), m\_ppl\,(.06) \\
78	GPT-2\,XL, $\tau$  & \textbf{p90\_ppl\,(.25)}, \textbf{p75\,(.15)}, m\_surp\,(.13), var\_surp\,(.12), p50\,(.05) \\
79	GPT-2\,XL, top-$k$ & \textbf{p90\_ppl\,(.24)}, \textbf{p75\,(.12)}, var\_surp\,(.10), m\_surp\,(.09), ttr\,(.04) \\
80	OLMo, nuc.         & \textbf{p90\_ppl\,(.18)}, \textbf{var\_surp\,(.15)}, p75\,(.11), m\_surp\,(.07), ttr\,(.06) \\
81	OLMo, $\tau$       & \textbf{p90\_ppl\,(.21)}, \textbf{var\_surp\,(.16)}, p75\,(.12), m\_surp\,(.09), ttr\,(.05) \\
82	OLMo, top-$k$      & \textbf{p90\_ppl\,(.20)}, \textbf{var\_surp\,(.17)}, p75\,(.10), m\_surp\,(.07), m\_ppl\,(.05) \\
83	\bottomrule
84	\end{tabular}}
85	\end{table}
86	
87	\begin{figure}[t]
88	\centering
89	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_atlas_heatmap.pdf}
90	\caption{Atlas feature importance heatmap. Rows: 19 features grouped by category (\S\ref{sec:method:features}); columns: 9 model--strategy cells. Color intensity encodes RF Gini importance. The perplexity-tail and surprisal-variance blocks maintain high importance across all cells.}
91	\label{fig:atlas_heatmap}
92	\end{figure}
93	
94	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
95	\subsection{Monotonicity and Inter-Depth Distances}
96	\label{sec:atlas:monotonicity}
97	
98	Depth features exhibit strong monotonic trends: perplexity tail statistics (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{mean\_surprisal}) decrease with depth (Spearman $\rho = -1.0$ across cell-level medians) while repetition features increase, reflecting the complementary narrowing and self-repetition of distribution collapse.
99	Inter-depth distances are non-uniform: d0-vs-d1 AUC exceeds 0.99 in all 9 cells, whereas d2-vs-d3 ranges from 0.69 to 0.89; separating adjacent deep generations requires the tail statistics identified in \S\ref{sec:atlas:features}.
100	
101	\begin{figure}[t]
102	\centering
103	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_feature_trajectory.pdf}
104	\caption{Feature trajectories across depths $d{=}0$ to $d{=}3$, stratified by model (columns) and strategy (line style). Top row: \texttt{p90\_ppl} (monotonically decreasing). Middle: \texttt{var\_surprisal} (decreasing). Bottom: \texttt{rep\_3gram} (increasing). Shaded bands: interquartile range. The $d{=}0 \to d{=}1$ gap exceeds all subsequent inter-depth gaps.}
105	\label{fig:feature_trajectory}
106	\end{figure}
107	
108	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
109	\subsection{EDD Analysis}
110	\label{sec:atlas:edd}
111	
112	We extend the benchmark to depth $d{=}5$ for all three models under nucleus sampling.
113	Each model's depth-3 LoRA checkpoint is used to finetune and generate depth-4 data, and the process repeats for depth~5; feature extraction uses the same reference model (Pythia-1.4B).
114	We train dedicated binary RF classifiers (500 trees) for each adjacent pair, as defined in Eq.~\ref{eq:edd}.
115	
116	\paragraph{AUC decay profile.}
117	Figure~\ref{fig:auc_decay} plots the binary pairwise AUC decay curves.
118	For Pythia-1.4B (nucleus), AUC decays monotonically: d0-vs-d1 $= 0.999$, d1-vs-d2 $= 0.925$, d2-vs-d3 $= 0.823$, d3-vs-d4 $= 0.784$, d4-vs-d5 $= 0.683$.
119	The steepest drop occurs between the d1-vs-d2 and d2-vs-d3 pairs; the curve then flattens as the system approaches an indistinguishable regime gradually rather than crossing a sharp boundary.
120	
121	\paragraph{Cross-model convergence at depth 4--5.}
122	The d3-vs-d4 AUC consistently clusters near the $T{=}0.75$ threshold across all three models (Pythia $0.784$, OLMo $0.765$, GPT-2~XL $0.750$), while d4-vs-d5 uniformly falls below $0.70$ ($0.681$--$0.684$).
123	The directional pattern is consistent, but statistical strength is stratified: bootstrap testing ($10{,}000$ resamples, $H_0{:}\, \mathrm{AUC} \leq 0.75$) yields $p = 0.001$ for Pythia (significant), $p = 0.091$ for OLMo (marginal), and $p = 0.505$ for GPT-2~XL (non-significant).
124	All three models cross the $T{=}0.75$ threshold within the d3--d4 region, establishing a consistent depth-4 decay boundary with graded confidence rather than uniform statistical significance.
125	The d4-vs-d5 saturation is unambiguous across models, supporting the interpretation of d3--d4 as a \emph{transition zone} from discriminable to indistinguishable regime.
126	
127	\paragraph{EDD threshold sensitivity.}
128	Table~\ref{tab:edd_sensitivity} reports $\mathrm{EDD}_T$ across the primary 9-cell benchmark (depths 0--3) at four threshold values.
129	At $T{=}0.65$, all 9 cells achieve $\mathrm{EDD} = 3$; at $T{=}0.75$, 7 of 9 cells maintain $\mathrm{EDD} \geq 3$; at $T{=}0.80$, the count drops to 5 of 9.
130	The cells losing $\mathrm{EDD}{=}3$ first are consistently the top-$k$ configurations (Pythia top-$k$ at $T{=}0.70$, then OLMo top-$k$ at $T{=}0.75$), where the d2-vs-d3 pair is the consistent bottleneck across all 9 cells.
131	
132	\begin{table}[t]
133	\centering
134	\small
135	\caption{Number of atlas cells achieving $\mathrm{EDD} \geq 3$ at each threshold $T$, across 9 model--strategy cells (depths 0--3). The d2-vs-d3 boundary is the bottleneck; top-$k$ cells drop first.}
136	\label{tab:edd_sensitivity}
137	\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccc@{}}
138	\toprule
139	& $T{=}0.65$ & $T{=}0.70$ & $T{=}0.75$ & $T{=}0.80$ \\
140	\midrule
141	Cells with $\mathrm{EDD} \geq 3$ & 9/9 & 8/9 & 7/9 & 5/9 \\
142	\bottomrule
143	\end{tabular}
144	\end{table}
145	
146	\begin{figure}[t]
147	\centering
148	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_auc_decay.pdf}
149	\caption{Binary pairwise AUC decay curves for three models (nucleus sampling, depths 0--5). Horizontal dashed lines mark $T \in \{0.65, 0.70, 0.75, 0.80\}$. All three curves converge below 0.70 at d4-vs-d5, while d3-vs-d4 AUC clusters in the range 0.750--0.784. Shaded bands: bootstrap 95\% CIs.}
150	\label{fig:auc_decay}
151	\end{figure}
152	
153	\paragraph{Decision boundary dilution.}
154	\label{sec:atlas:edd:dilution}
155	EDD uses binary-pair classifiers to avoid \emph{decision boundary dilution}: in Pythia nucleus, d2\,vs.\,d3 AUC degrades from 0.804 (4-class) to 0.689 (6-class), a 14.3\% relative decline despite identical data, because shared decision boundaries dilute per-pair capacity.
156	Binary classifiers eliminate this confound, isolating true adjacent-pair discriminability.
157	
158	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
159	\subsection{Strategy-Dependent Trajectories}
160	\label{sec:atlas:strategy}
161	
162	The three decoding strategies induce qualitatively distinct degradation trajectories.
163	Nucleus ($p{=}0.95$) produces the most consistent accuracy (78.2--83.3\%) and serves as the reference trajectory.
164	Temperature ($\tau{=}0.9$) yields the highest accuracy in 2/3 models (GPT-2~XL 85.4\%, OLMo 82.0\%) because uniform logit scaling accelerates convergence to an attractor distribution~\cite{shumailov2024_nature}, amplifying the statistical fingerprint. However, this acceleration creates a boundary reversal risk: temperature depth-$N$ features approximate nucleus/top-$k$ depth-$(N{+}1)$ features, causing cross-strategy classifiers to systematically overpredict depth (\S\ref{sec:generalization}).
165	Top-$k$ ($k{=}50$) produces the lowest accuracy (69.6--76.6\%) because hard vocabulary truncation removes depth-discriminative low-probability tokens, though feature direction is preserved (cross-model $\rho = 0.811$).
166	The strategy effect (8.4~pp range) exceeds the model effect (7.1~pp), indicating deployment-time knowledge of the decoding strategy matters at least as much as the generator model.
167

2	As large language models increasingly train on web text containing their own outputs, a recursive model$\to$data$\to$model loop arises, yet no method estimates how many such iterations a text has undergone.
3	We formalize \emph{recursive generation depth estimation} as ordinal classification and construct a benchmark of 180K passages spanning 3 model families, 3 decoding strategies, and 4 generation depths.
4	A Random Forest over 19 perplexity-based features achieves 70--85\% four-class accuracy (chance = 25\%), with perplexity tail statistics emerging as consistent depth markers; a parsimonious subset of 5 features retains 97.6\% of full performance.
5	We define the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric, finding $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.75}{=}4$ for the best-characterized family, and show that cross-model transfer reaches 66.4\% (2.7$\times$ chance).
6	Systematic generalization across seven axes (including cross-scale with 7B models at 70.2\%, cross-domain, and LoRA-rank ablation) confirms that depth signal is robust and resides in distributional statistics inaccessible from surface text (zero-shot LLMs: 30--36\%, 42\,pp below RF).
7	\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

The text on which large language models are trained increasingly contains their own outputs.
As synthetic content proliferates across the web, a recursive loop emerges: models trained on web corpora ingest text generated by earlier models, and their outputs feed into the next generation's training data \cite{shumailov2024_nature,alemohammad2024_mad}.
This model$\to$data$\to$model cycle is no longer hypothetical; it is already occurring in the wild. Yet we lack the ability to determine how many recursive iterations a given text has undergone, a distinction that matters because first-generation synthetic text may be benign or even beneficial for training, while deeply recursive text drives the distributional collapse that degrades model quality \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails}.

Existing tools address adjacent but distinct problems.
Binary detectors such as Binoculars \cite{binoculars2024}, Fast-DetectGPT \cite{fast_detectgpt2024}, and DivEye \cite{diveye2026} classify text as human-written or machine-generated, collapsing all depths $d \geq 1$ into a single category.
Watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark} requires proactive embedding and cannot be applied retroactively.
The model collapse literature \cite{shumailov2024_nature,dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails} assumes depth is known a priori; \citet{drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse} filter synthetic data via binary detection without distinguishing depths.
No existing method estimates the ordinal recursive generation depth of a text passage from its content alone.

We find that recursive generation leaves quantifiable statistical fingerprints in text, and these fingerprints are \textbf{consistent in direction but scale-dependent in magnitude} across the three model families and three decoding strategies studied.
Specifically, perplexity tail statistics (the 90th-percentile perplexity, \textsc{p90\_ppl}, and surprisal variance, \textsc{var\_surprisal}) emerge as dominant depth indicators, ranking in the top two features by importance in 9/9 and 8/9 model--strategy configurations, respectively.
Instruction-tuned variants exhibit monotonically decreasing AUC (regularization), whereas base models can show non-monotonic trajectories, suggesting that instruction tuning acts as a regularizer on the depth signal rather than introducing degradation.

We formalize recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification and introduce a lightweight pipeline: compute 19 reference-model perplexity features (effective dimensionality ${\approx}$4--5 due to multicollinearity; \S\ref{sec:atlas:features}) and classify with a Random Forest into $K{+}1$ depth classes.
To characterize how recursive generation reshapes these features, we construct the \emph{Depth Degradation Atlas}: a $3 \times 3$ grid of model families $\times$ decoding strategies spanning 4 depths (180K samples).
The atlas reveals strategy-dependent degradation trajectories and we introduce the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric to quantify how far into the recursion chain adjacent depths remain distinguishable.

Our contributions are:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Task formalization and benchmark.} We define recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification, introduce the EDD metric, and construct a 180K-sample benchmark spanning 3 model families $\times$ 3 decoding strategies $\times$ 4 depths.

    \item \textbf{Depth Degradation Atlas.} A systematic $3 \times 3$ characterization reveals that perplexity tail statistics dominate depth discrimination (top-2 in 9/9 and 8/9 cells), decoding strategy reshapes degradation trajectories qualitatively, and $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.75}{=}4$ for the best-characterized family (Pythia, $p{=}0.001$; consistent across all three families).

    \item \textbf{Generalization across seven axes.} Cross-model recursive chains (84.75\%), cross-scale observations on two 7B models (70.2\% and 60.1\%), cross-domain transfer (arXiv 74.1\%), temperature robustness ($\tau \in [0.5, 0.9]$), and reference model robustness (67--79\% accuracy across three reference models). A surface-text ablation (zero-shot LLMs at 30--36\%, 42\,pp below RF) confirms the signal resides in distributional statistics, while requiring only 19 features and a Random Forest for GPU-free inference.
\end{itemize}

1	\section{Method}
2	\label{sec:method}
3	
4	\subsection{Problem Definition}
5	\label{sec:method:problem}
6	
7	Let $f_\theta$ denote a language model and $\mathcal{D}_0$ a corpus of human-written seed text.
8	We define a \emph{recursive generation chain} of depth $K$ as the sequence $\mathcal{D}_0, \mathcal{D}_1, \dots, \mathcal{D}_K$, where each $\mathcal{D}_k$ ($k \geq 1$) is produced by finetuning $f_\theta$ on $\mathcal{D}_{k-1}$ and sampling from the resulting model.
9	Depth $d{=}0$ denotes human-written text; depth $d{=}k$ ($k \geq 1$) denotes text generated by a model trained on depth-$(k{-}1)$ data.
10	
11	Given a text passage $x$, the task is to estimate its recursive generation depth $d \in \{0, 1, \dots, K\}$.
12	This is an ordinal classification problem: depths carry a natural ordering, and $d{=}1$ is structurally closer to $d{=}0$ than $d{=}3$ is, since each generation step compounds distributional drift.
13	
14	\subsection{Multi-Generational Benchmark Construction}
15	\label{sec:method:benchmark}
16	
17	We construct a benchmark spanning three axes: model family, decoding strategy, and generation depth.
18	
19	\paragraph{Model families.}
20	We select three 1--1.5B-parameter models with diverse pretraining corpora and architectures: Pythia-1.4B (EleutherAI), OLMo-1B (AI2), and GPT-2~XL (OpenAI, 1.5B).
21	Restricting to a narrow parameter range isolates the effect of architecture and training data from scale.
22	
23	\paragraph{Decoding strategies.}
24	Each model is paired with three decoding strategies: nucleus sampling ($p{=}0.95$) \cite{holtzman2020_nucleus}, temperature sampling ($\tau{=}0.9$), and top-$k$ sampling ($k{=}50$).
25	These span the dominant modes of open-ended generation and induce qualitatively different entropy profiles.
26	Our findings on feature importance and discriminability are limited to this grid; transfer to untested models, scales, or strategies is not established.
27	
28	\paragraph{Depth and scale.}
29	The primary benchmark covers depths d0--d3 across all $3 \times 3 = 9$ model--strategy cells, with 5{,}000 samples per depth per cell (180K samples total).
30	For depth extension experiments (\S\ref{sec:atlas}), we extend one pipeline (Pythia-1.4B, nucleus) to d0--d5.
31	
32	\paragraph{Generation pipeline.}
33	Starting from a Wikipedia subset as seed text ($\mathcal{D}_0$), each generation cycle proceeds in three steps: (1)~LoRA finetuning \cite{hu2022lora} on $\mathcal{D}_{k-1}$, freezing base model weights and training low-rank update matrices ($<$1\% additional parameters; $r{=}16$, $\alpha{=}32$, lr $2{\times}10^{-4}$, batch size 8, 3 epochs, dropout $0.05$, architecture-specific targets); (2)~sampling 5{,}000 passages from the LoRA-finetuned model (max 512 tokens, BOS-seeded, no prompt conditioning) under the specified decoding strategy; (3)~the generated corpus becomes $\mathcal{D}_k$ for the next cycle.
34	Each depth is produced by a model explicitly trained on the prior depth's data, not by sampling from the unmodified base model.
35	Our BOS-seeded generation may amplify depth signal relative to prompted settings; extending to prompt-conditioned generation is future work.
36	There is no per-passage lineage across depths, ensuring cross-validation splits do not introduce information leakage.
37	
38	\paragraph{Reference model.}
39	All statistical features (\S\ref{sec:method:features}) are computed using Pythia-1.4B as fixed reference model, the smallest generator whose training corpus partially overlaps with the others.
40	For Pythia this constitutes self-model measurement, yet its accuracy (78.2\%) does not exceed GPT-2~XL (85.4\%), indicating no systematic self-model advantage.
41	Ablations with OLMo-1B and GPT-2 XL as alternative references yield 67--79\% accuracy (Appendix~\ref{app:ref_ablation}), confirming reference model robustness; further discussion in Limitations.
42	
43	\subsection{Statistical Feature Design}
44	\label{sec:method:features}
45	
46	We extract a feature vector $\mathbf{f}(x)$ comprising 19 candidate features from the reference-model perplexity distribution over each passage $x$; ablation (\S\ref{sec:atlas:features}) shows the top 5 achieve 97.6\% of full-set performance, and variance inflation analysis reveals VIF${>}$10 for 14--16 features, placing the effective independent dimensionality at ${\approx}$4--5.
47	The features fall into four categories (Table~\ref{tab:features}).
48	
49	\begin{table}[t]
50	\centering
51	\small
52	\caption{The 19 statistical features comprising $\mathbf{f}(x)$, grouped by category. All perplexity and surprisal features are computed from the reference model (Pythia-1.4B).}
53	\label{tab:features}
54	\begin{tabular}{@{}llr@{}}
55	\toprule
56	Category & Features & $n$ \\
57	\midrule
58	Perplexity & mean, var, skewness, kurtosis, & 9 \\
59	statistics & p10, p25, p50, p75, p90 & \\
60	\addlinespace
61	Surprisal & mean, var, entropy & 3 \\
62	statistics & & \\
63	\addlinespace
64	Lexical & type--token ratio, hapax ratio, & 4 \\
65	diversity & bigram entropy, trigram entropy & \\
66	\addlinespace
67	Repetition & repeated 2/3/4-gram fractions & 3 \\
68	\bottomrule
69	\end{tabular}
70	\end{table}
71	
72	\emph{Perplexity statistics} (9 features) capture the per-token perplexity distribution via moments (mean, variance, skewness, kurtosis) and quantiles (p10--p90); tail quantiles prove especially informative as recursive finetuning erodes the high-perplexity tail (\S\ref{sec:atlas}).
73	\emph{Surprisal statistics} (3 features): mean, variance, and entropy of $-\log p(\text{token})$; surprisal variance captures second-order structure not redundant with perplexity moments.
74	\emph{Lexical diversity} (4 features): type--token ratio, hapax ratio, bigram/trigram entropy.
75	\emph{Repetition} (3 features): repeated $n$-gram fractions for $n \in \{2, 3, 4\}$.
76	
77	\subsection{Effective Discriminable Depth}
78	\label{sec:method:edd}
79	
80	Aggregate multi-class accuracy obscures whether discriminability degrades at specific depth boundaries.
81	We introduce the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) to formalize the frontier beyond which adjacent depths become statistically indistinguishable.
82	
83	\paragraph{Pairwise discriminability.}
84	Let $\mathcal{D} = \{0, 1, \dots, K\}$ denote the depth set and $T \in (0.5, 1.0]$ a discrimination threshold.
85	For each adjacent pair $(d, d{+}1)$, we define the pairwise discriminability $\mathrm{AUC}(d, d{+}1)$ as the area under the ROC curve of a dedicated binary Random Forest classifier (500 trees, $\lfloor\sqrt{19}\rfloor$ candidate features per split) trained on class-balanced data from $\mathbf{f}(x)$ (\S\ref{sec:method:features}) to distinguish depth-$d$ from depth-$(d{+}1)$ samples, evaluated via 5-fold stratified cross-validation.
86	Each pair uses an independent classifier, avoiding the decision boundary dilution that arises in multi-class settings (\S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}).
87	
88	\begin{definition}[Effective Discriminable Depth]
89	\label{def:edd}
90	The \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} at threshold $T$ is:
91	\begin{equation}
92	\mathrm{EDD}_T = \max \bigl\{ d^*{+}1 \,:\, \forall\, d' \leq d^*,\; \mathrm{AUC}(d', d'{+}1) \geq T \bigr\}
93	\label{eq:edd}
94	\end{equation}
95	where $d^* \in \{0, \dots, K{-}1\}$. If\, $\mathrm{AUC}(0,1) < T$, then $\mathrm{EDD}_T = 0$.
96	\end{definition}
97	
98	$\mathrm{EDD}_T$ is the deepest depth $d$ such that every adjacent pair from $(0,1)$ through $(d{-}1, d)$ remains discriminable at level $T$.
99	The universal quantifier ensures EDD reports the longest \emph{contiguous} discriminable prefix rather than an isolated high-AUC pair at greater depth.\footnote{Our AUC profiles are empirically monotonically decreasing for the 1--1.5B base models (\S\ref{sec:atlas}), so in practice $\mathrm{EDD}_T = \max\{d'{+}1 : \mathrm{AUC}(d', d'{+}1) \geq T\}$. Qwen2.5-7B exhibits a U-shaped AUC pattern rather than monotonic decay; a base-model control shows non-monotonic decay persists without instruction tuning (\S\ref{sec:gen:crossscale}). For non-monotonic profiles, the contiguous formulation is more conservative (see Limitations).}
100	We set $T{=}0.75$ as default; sensitivity at $T \in \{0.65, 0.70, 0.75, 0.80\}$ is reported in \S\ref{sec:atlas}.
101	
102	\paragraph{Classifiers.}
103	Our primary classifier is a Random Forest (200 trees, unconstrained depth, 5-fold stratified cross-validation).
104	We compare against CORAL ordinal regression \cite{coral2020}, DivEye \cite{diveye2026}, a 2-layer cross-entropy MLP, logistic regression, and a single-feature baseline using mean perplexity alone; results appear in \S\ref{sec:generalization}.

1	\section{Generalization and Robustness}
2	\label{sec:generalization}
3	
4	We test whether atlas accuracy (69.6--85.4\%) reflects genuine statistical regularities, evaluating along seven axes: four below (\S\ref{sec:gen:baselines}--\S\ref{sec:gen:crossscale}) and three in the Appendix (end-to-end learning, temperature robustness, cross-boundary transfer).
5	
6	\subsection{Classifier Comparison and Surface-Text Ablation}
7	\label{sec:gen:baselines}
8	
9	Table~\ref{tab:baselines} evaluates bagging (RF) and gradient boosting (XGBoost, LightGBM) on the same 19 features; per-cell spread is $\leq$0.4pp, establishing a feature-determined ceiling.
10	On Pythia nucleus, CORAL ordinal regression \cite{coral2020} (78.1\%) and DivEye \cite{diveye2026} (78.2\%) match the within-cell RF of Table~\ref{tab:main_matrix} within 0.1\,pp (bootstrap $p>0.05$, Bonferroni-corrected); all feature-based methods significantly outperform CE-MLP (74.9\%, $p<0.001$) and logistic regression (75.0\%).
11	
12	\paragraph{Surface-text ablation.}
13	Single-feature regression on mean perplexity performs at chance (25.1\%); two zero-shot LLMs (DeepSeek V3.2, 36.2\%; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, 30.4\%; each 500 samples, prompt in Appendix~\ref{app:zeroshot_prompt}) also fail, confirming that the depth signal resides in distributional statistics inaccessible from surface text alone (42\,pp gap vs.\ RF at 78.2\%).

89	Mean cross-strategy accuracy (59.1\%) falls 7pp below cross-model transfer (66.4\%); excluding d0, d1--d3 accuracy drops to 45.9\% (chance = 33\%).
90	d2 recall varies sharply: nucleus holdouts retain 30--54\%, top-$k$ holdouts fall to 8--19\%, and temperature holdouts span 3.7--39.5\% (median 8.9\%).
91	Training on nucleus + top-$k$ and testing on temperature inverts the d1/d2 boundary (d1v2 AUC $<$ 0.5); per-strategy z-score normalization partially recovers it but leaves a residual gap (Limitations).
92	A multi-temperature ablation (Appendix~\ref{app:multi_tau}) confirms that within-$\tau$ depth signal holds for $\tau \leq 0.9$ (d1v2 AUC $>0.80$, accuracy within 3pp of $\tau{=}0.7$) but collapses at $\tau{=}1.1$; cross-$\tau$ LOO transfer (mean 46.7\%) is harder than cross-strategy transfer.
93	
94	End-to-end PLMs (DeBERTa-v3, RoBERTa) achieve only ${\sim}$59\%, lagging RF by 19pp, confirming depth signal is inaccessible to standard PLM representations (Appendix~\ref{app:e2e}).

97	\subsection{Preliminary Cross-Scale Observations}
98	\label{sec:gen:crossscale}
99	
100	To test whether depth signal persists at larger scale, we extend the benchmark to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct~\cite{qwen2.5} and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct~\cite{llama3} under 4-bit NF4 QLoRA (nucleus $p{=}0.95$, 500 samples/depth, depths 0--5).
101	Both models exceed chance: Llama-3.1-8B achieves 70.2\% (95\% CI $[68.3, 72.4]$, $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}4$) and Qwen2.5-7B 60.1\% ($[58.0, 62.1]$, $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{>}5$), with weaker per-step signal than 1--1.5B models (mean consecutive AUC ${\approx}$0.78 vs.\ 0.85).
102	The two instruction-tuned models exhibit divergent AUC trajectories: Llama-3.1-8B decays monotonically (consistent with 1--1.5B), while Qwen2.5-7B shows a U-shaped recovery.
103	
104	\paragraph{Base vs.\ Instruction-Tuned Control.}
105	A base-model control (Llama-3.1-8B) achieves 59.9\% with non-monotonic AUC decay, while the instruction-tuned variant reaches 70.2\% with strictly monotonic decay, suggesting instruction-tuning \emph{regularizes} recursive degradation patterns rather than introducing confounding artifacts.
106	
107	Four confounds (quantization, reduced $n$, single strategy, vocabulary mismatch) limit causal attribution; full results including per-pair AUC tables appear in Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale_full}.
108	Cross-model recursive chains (84.75\%), validated by a reverse-chain control (85.75\%; Appendix~\ref{app:cross_boundary}), and cross-domain transfer (arXiv 74.1\%) further confirm signal universality.
109	
110	\paragraph{LoRA rank sensitivity.}
111	Depth signal persists across LoRA ranks 4--64 (accuracy spread 4.65\,pp; Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale_full}), confirming the phenomenon is not an artifact of a specific fine-tuning configuration.

1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	We formalized recursive generation depth estimation and showed that perplexity tail statistics achieve 70--85\% four-class accuracy ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.75}{=}4$), with five features sufficing for 97.6\% of full performance and classifier-agnostic convergence within $\leq$0.4pp.
5	These features generalize across model families without retraining, positioning depth estimation as an early-warning signal for model collapse~\cite{shumailov2024_nature,shi2025_closer_look}; zero-shot LLMs at 30--36\% (\S\ref{sec:gen:baselines}) confirm the signal is inaccessible from surface text alone.
6	Cross-strategy transfer remains the primary bottleneck; see Limitations for detailed analysis.
7	Depth-graduated curation complements binary detection~\cite{dsir2023,qurating2024} and watermarking~\cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark} as a provenance signal~\cite{bevendorff2025_two_paradigms}; pilot results are inconclusive (Appendix~\ref{app:curation_poc}) and adversarial robustness remains untested.
8

1	\section{Additional Results}
2	\label{app:additional}
3	
4	\subsection{Top-$k$ Feature Trajectories}
5	\label{app:topk_trajectories}
6	
7	Figure~\ref{fig:feature_trajectory} in the main text shows feature trajectories for nucleus ($p{=}0.95$) and temperature ($\tau{=}0.9$) sampling.
8	Top-$k$ ($k{=}50$) trajectories follow the same monotonically decreasing trend for all features but with compressed inter-depth spacing, consistent with the signal attenuation effect discussed in \S\ref{sec:atlas:strategy}.
9	Concretely, the d0$\to$d1 drop in \textsc{p90\_ppl} under top-$k$ is 78\% (vs.\ 87\% for nucleus), and the d2$\to$d3 reduction is 31\% (vs.\ 39\% for nucleus).
10	Despite the magnitude reduction, feature rank ordering across depths is preserved, which explains why ordinal classifiers maintain directionality even under top-$k$ conditions.
11	
12	\subsection{Permutation Importance}
13	\label{app:permutation}
14	
15	To verify that the Gini-based importance rankings in \S\ref{sec:atlas:features} are not an artifact of the impurity measure, we compute permutation importance (5-fold CV, 10 repeats) for all 9 atlas cells.
16	The top-2 features are stable across measures: \textsc{p90\_ppl} ranks in the top 2 in 9/9 cells under both Gini and permutation importance, and \textsc{var\_surprisal} in 8/9 (vs.\ 7/9 for Gini, with the additional cell being OLMo top-$k$; the single SHAP exception is GPT-2~XL top-$k$, where \textsc{p75\_ppl} displaces \textsc{var\_surprisal} to rank 3).
17	Kendall's $W{=}0.90$ across all three methods (Gini, permutation, SHAP) indicates strong concordance ($p{<}0.005$).
18	Pairwise Spearman correlations are: SHAP--Gini $\rho{=}0.93$, SHAP--permutation $\rho{=}0.84$, Gini--permutation $\rho{=}0.76$.
19	Per-cell top-5 overlap between SHAP and permutation importance is 3--4 out of 5 features; the aggregated (mean-across-cells) top-5 sets are identical, confirming that the top features are robust to the choice of importance measure at the aggregate level while per-cell rankings exhibit model-dependent variation.
